title: Foods to Limit or Cook Thoroughly During Pregnancy
excerpt: Food-safety guidance inspired by CDC/NHS/FDA themes: deli meats, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to choose safe and healthy foods to ensure the well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we'll provide information on foods that pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly to avoid health risks.

## Foods to Limit
According to reputable sources like the CDC, NHS, and FDA, there are certain foods that pregnant women should limit or avoid during pregnancy. Here are some examples:

* Deli meats and hot dogs: These foods can contain Listeria bacteria, which can harm the fetus.
* Unpasteurized dairy products: Unpasteurized dairy products can contain E. coli and Salmonella bacteria, which can harm both mother and baby.
* High-mercury fish: Fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel can contain high levels of mercury, which can harm fetal development.
* Undercooked or raw foods: Undercooked or raw foods like sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs can contain Salmonella and E. coli bacteria, which can harm both mother and baby.

## Foods to Cook Thoroughly
To ensure food safety, pregnant women should cook the following foods thoroughly:

* Chicken and beef: Cook chicken and beef to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to avoid Salmonella and E. coli bacteria.
* Fish and seafood: Cook fish and seafood to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C) to avoid Salmonella and E. coli bacteria.
* Eggs: Cook eggs to an internal temperature of at least 160°F (71°C) to avoid Salmonella bacteria.

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips to help pregnant women choose safe and healthy foods:

* Read food labels: When buying food, read the labels to know the ingredients and storage instructions.
* Choose fresh foods: Choose fresh foods and avoid processed or stored foods.
* Cook food thoroughly: Cook food thoroughly to avoid bacteria and health risks.
* Consult a healthcare provider: If you have any questions about food, consult a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian.

## When to Seek Help
If you experience any of the following symptoms, seek help from a healthcare provider:

* High fever
* Abdominal pain
* Diarrhea
* Vomiting

Remember, choosing safe and healthy foods is crucial to ensuring the well-being of both mother and baby. If you have any questions, consult a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian.

faqs.question: Are deli meats safe for pregnant women?
faqs.answer: No, deli meats can contain Listeria bacteria, which can harm the fetus.

faqs.question: Can high-mercury fish harm the fetus?

faqs.question: How should I cook chicken and beef to avoid foodborne illness?
